lyrics:
[Intro: solo piano, rolling arpeggio pattern]

[Verse 1: low, plain, piano only]
I heard you painted the kitchen
The yellow we never chose
I heard you got a dog now
And it sleeps across your toes
I heard you're up at six these days
You never were for me
It's funny what a person keeps
For whoever comes to be

[Pre-Chorus: voice rises, piano fuller]
I wasn't going to call, I wasn't going to write
I only want you knowing that I know, and it's alright

[Chorus: full voice, raw at the top, piano rolling]
Good for you
I mean it, good for you
I'll find my own shade of yellow
I'll paint a room or two
And if you're ever passing
You don't have to call
Some things don't end, they only dry
Like colour on a wall

[Verse 2: low, a little warmer]
I kept the chair you hated
I learned to like the cold
I say your mother's sayings
I am getting, somehow, old
I saw a man in your old coat
Outside the corner shop
And all the years came running back
And then I made them stop

[Pre-Chorus: voice rises, piano fuller]
I wasn't going to call, I wasn't going to write
I only want you knowing that I know, and it's alright

[Chorus: full voice, raw at the top, piano rolling]
Good for you
I mean it, good for you
I'll find my own shade of yellow
I'll paint a room or two
And if you're ever passing
You don't have to call
Some things don't end, they only dry
Like colour on a wall

[Bridge: piano drops to single chords, voice exposed]
Nothing sticks like the first coat
Nobody tells you that
You cover it and cover it
And it's still under there

[Final Chorus: softer start, then the biggest held note]
Good for you
I mean it, good for you
I'll find my own shade of yellow
I'll paint a room or two
And if you're ever passing
You don't have to call
Some things don't end, they only dry
Like colour on a wall

[Outro: piano pattern slows, last line almost spoken]
Like colour on a wall
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 67 BPM, 4/4, A major. A slow, rolling piano pattern that keeps turning like a wheel. Bare and dignified.

VOICE: Female contralto, rich and smoky low down, with a London accent in the vowels. Verses sung plainly and close. In the chorus she pushes into a powerful upper range that frays and cracks at the very top. The last line is nearly spoken. No backing vocals.

INSTRUMENTS: One acoustic piano and nothing else. The right hand plays a continuous broken-chord pattern, the left hand plain bass notes. In the bridge it reduces to single held chords.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the piano pattern. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:57 Pre-chorus. 1:12 Chorus 1. 1:41 Verse 2. 2:24 Pre-chorus. 2:38 Chorus 2. 3:07 Bridge, single chords. 3:25 Final chorus, starting softly and reaching the biggest held note on the seventh line. 3:54 Outro, the pattern slows and the last line is half spoken at 4:02.

PRODUCTION & MIX: A live-sounding piano ballad: close microphones, natural room, no effects. You can hear the pedal and the breaths.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The crack in the voice at the top of the first chorus.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original, written at twenty-one, cannot yet wish him well. This narrator can, and the bridge explains how: the first coat is still under there, and she has stopped needing to cover it.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Curiosity, a pang, generosity, peace.
